findings.message: This file has two `clutch:meta` headers, at lines 2-9 and again at lines 11-18, and their hashes differ (71f7dd71... and 50f211d0...). Scope in requires the file to start with one header from `clutch meta refresh` with only `purpose` edited by hand. The second block is a stale extra copy that `meta` does not parse as the header.
findings.paved_road: Delete the duplicate block at lines 11-18 and run `uv run clutch meta refresh tests/integration/test_serve_scan_watch_overlap.py`, so the file carries exactly one header with a current hash.

findings.message: This file also has two `clutch:meta` headers, at lines 2-9 and lines 11-18, with different hashes (07424e10... and 2cb6fab7...). The extra block is a stale copy left in the module.
findings.paved_road: Delete the duplicate block at lines 11-18 and run `uv run clutch meta refresh tests/unit/test_serve_scan_watch_locks.py`.

findings.message: The reproducer's header was copied from tests/regress_serve_parallel_admission.py: its purpose reads "Reproduce idle poll blocking parallel admission.", and the docstring calls it an idle scan. The script actually reproduces a changed-snapshot scan entering the exclusive section while a run holds a slot. Scope in requires a header from `clutch meta refresh` with a `purpose` that describes this file.
findings.paved_road: Regenerate the header with `uv run clutch meta refresh tests/regress_serve_scan_watch_off_exclusive.py`. Then set `purpose` and the docstring to say a changed scan must not wait on a held run slot.

findings.message: Criterion 2 requires the stop request made while a run is held to be honored, not dropped. The test only waits until `control.projection.stop_requested` is set. Its `finally` then calls `finish`, which calls `rig.owner.stop()` itself. So serve shutting down is never shown to come from the held-time request: a request that is projected but never acted on would still pass.
findings.paved_road: After the request is projected, assert that no new implementation starts. Then set `release` and wait until `run.done()` without calling `owner.stop()`, so serve ends because of the stop request itself. Check the exit code and active.json the way `finish` does.

findings.message: Criterion 3 requires showing `scan` with one run holding a slot. `test_scan_lock_and_stop` runs against the fixture's recording admission and never holds a run slot. So it never shows that a changed scan finishes while a run is held.
findings.paved_road: Hold a run slot before the changed scan, either through a real `DaemonAdmission` dispatch blocked on an event or by marking the fixture admission as holding. Then assert that `scan` completes, `owner.entries == []`, and the reads happen under `main_write()`.
